doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: College listening to Ives and Cage; last seeing Armstrong
summary: At college Jordan listened to Ives, Cage and Stockhausen while friends held a jam session, and once left a Cage concert to see Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So going back to college for a minute. You’re exploring all these things. You’re kind of doing that on your own apart from your education studies.

Oh yeah definitely. I remember one time they had a big jam session and homecoming, Ellis Marsalis and Alvin Batiste and all of them was down. And I was over at the library listening at John Cage and who else — oh it’s slipped my mind — well Stockhausen too but there was a classical composer, Ives, I was listening to Ives. And they thought I was listening to Burl Ives. I said, “Man, I was in the library listening to Ives.” “Oh you listen to Burl Ives? What’s wrong with you?” So I had to go along with it. So I came to the jam session and I was laughing because I was dead into that. And the last time I saw Louis Armstrong, Louis Armstrong played at the Loyola Field House and John Cage had a concert at Tulane. So I left from John Cage, early in the evening, to catch Louis Armstrong at the field house. So that was a whole day of stuff.
I’ll be darned. You have big ears.
